episodes.213682: Scattered thunderstorms once again developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours of July 11, 2026. A few of these thunderstorms became strong to briefly severe, resulting in several downed trees across the area.
episodes.213709: On the the late morning of the 11th, a moist and unstable airmass over central Indiana combined with a weak surface boundary to trigger convective development. Steering winds aloft were light, generally moving storms at speeds around 10 mph, which allowed the activity to remain nearly stationary over east-central portions of the state. This environment was highly favorable for efficient precipitation production, resulting in torrential rainfall rates before the storms dissipated in the early afternoon.||Between 11:00 AM and 1:00 PM EST, these slow-moving storms deposited 2 to 4 inches of rain across the Muncie area. The intense rainfall quickly overwhelmed local drainage infrastructure, resulting in significant flooding across multiple residential neighborhoods. Floodwaters completely submerged streets and parked vehicles, while also entering numerous houses. The water intrusion caused property damage, including ruined flooring and saturated interior walls. The indoor flooding also created hazardous conditions that resulted in one woman being hospitalized after suffering a fall inside her home.
episodes.213718: Monsoon moisture across eastern and southern New Mexico combined with daytime heating resulted in diurnal thunderstorm activity first across the higher terrain midday before moving into nearby lower elevations during the afternoon and evening hours on July 10th and 11th. Thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding and debris flow on and downstream of the burn scars surrounding Ruidoso both afternoons, and severe wind gusts near Ragland in Quay County the evening of July 10th and at two mesonet stations on White Sands Missile Range the evening of July 11th. Thunderstorms slowly diminished just before midnight both days.
episodes.213889: Ample instability and sufficient shear allowed for scattered showers and thunderstorms to begin developing across northeastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon hours of July 11, 2026. These storms continued to track south-southeastward throughout the afternoon and evening, bringing multiple rounds of heavy rainfall to the urban areas of Lebanon and Lancaster County. Some strong-to-severe thunderstorms stationed across eastern Pennsylvania moved into eastern Lebanon County initially, producing multiple instances of tree damage as it moved southward into northern Lancaster County. One instance of tree damage caused an injury, when a tree fell down onto a camper in the Cocalico Creek Campground and caused a head laceration to the occupant. Further south, thunderstorms weakened; however, locally heavy rainfall in Lancaster produced widespread flooding concerns, with multiple water rescues and roadways flooded east of the city.
episodes.213929: A cluster of thunderstorms that developed across the central portions of the Carolinas early in the afternoon merged into line segments that accelerated eastward and moved off the coast before evening. Numerous reports of strong wind gusts were received, especially in the Grand Strand area.
episodes.213930: A cluster of thunderstorms that developed across the central portions of the Carolinas early in the afternoon merged into line segments that accelerated eastward and moved off the coast before evening. Numerous reports of strong wind gusts were received, especially in the Grand Strand area.
episodes.213948: Upper level high pressure was centered to the west of the combined Panhandles. This allowed the region to be situated under northwest flow in the upper levels of the atmosphere, which tends to promote storms to move into the region from the northwest. As temperatures climbed into the upper 90s to lower 100s, the hot airmass combined with plenty of instability and the ability for storms to bring down wind energy from higher in the storm, storms that occurred were able to bring damaging winds to the region.
episodes.213949: As thunderstorms developed across portions of New Mexico and Colorado, they moved southeast along the eastern edge of an upper level high pressure system. These storms brought damaging winds with them given plenty of dry air aloft that could be brought down to the surface in the more severe storms.
episodes.214116: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the afternoon and evening of the 11th, near a stationary front that stretched across the region, as an upper level disturbance translated into the area. The strongest storms produced damaging wind in Washington County.
episodes.214117: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 11th, near a stationary front that stretched across the region, as an upper level disturbance translated into the area. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts and large hail to half dollar size.
episodes.214136: A stationary front stalled out across the Ohio Valley triggering showers and thunderstorms. Some storms produced gusty winds and heavy rainfall, resulting in flooding.
episodes.214187: Showers and thunderstorms fired along a stalled frontal boundary and produced heavy rainfall, leading to localized flooding.
episodes.214195: Showers and thunderstorms developed in a hot and humid airmass. Some storms produced damaging winds and locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.214213: Numerous thunderstorms developed through the evening hours due to an advancing cold front and very unstable atmosphere. Some of these storms became severe and produced instances of damaging winds.
episodes.214285: Mid level troughing interacted with a very moist and unstable environment the afternoon of 7/11 where PWATs were near 2 with surface-based CAPE values exceeding 3000 J/kg. This brought a cluster of severe storms across the Midlands of SC, extending into the CSRA, that caused extensive tree damage.
episodes.214286: Mid level troughing interacted with a very moist and unstable environment the afternoon of 7/11 where PWATs were near 2 with surface-based CAPE values exceeding 3000 J/kg. This brought a cluster of severe storms across the Midlands of SC, extending into the CSRA, that caused extensive tree damage.

episodes.214374: Low pressure and an associated warm front tracked through the Mid-Atlantic and produced heavy rain and subsequent flash flooding across portions of New Jersey and Pennsylvania.
episodes.214690: A stationary boundary was noted stalled across the state of Arkansas which led to much of central Arkansas experiencing damaging wind gusts, flash flooding, and excessive rainfall totals over a short period of time.
episodes.214845: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe. Unfortunately, two fatalities occurred in Tallahassee on July 10th when a large tree fell on a moving vehicle.
episodes.214947: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.214951: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms produced several wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.215271: Despite drier air aloft affecting portions of the area thanks to the Saharan Air Layer, enough moisture and instability was in place for scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms to develop across northeast FL. Southwest flow mainly focus isolated strong to severe convection over the eastern half of the region. Presence of dry air aloft likely played into stronger downbursts and areas of wind damage across northeast FL.
episodes.215456: Clusters of thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze in the afternoon hours along the southeast South Carolina coast. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts and hail into the early evening hours.
episodes.215463: Clusters of thunderstorms developed inland near the southeast South Carolina coast in the afternoon and early evening hours. These storms eventually moved into the Atlantic coastal waters through the late evening and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.215465: A large cluster of thunderstorms developed inland across the South Carolina Midlands in the early afternoon hours. These storms eventually moved across the South Carolina Lowcountry and into the Atlantic coastal waters, producing strong wind gusts into the early evening hours. A few additional storms developed along the southeast Georgia coast later in the evening and produced strong wind gusts further to the south.
episodes.215513: A cold front tracked eastwards across the Carolinas on July tenth. As this front neared the Coastal Plain, clusters of thunderstorms developed near the Inner Banks and tracked east during the afternoon and evening hours. With ample instability in place a few of these storms became strong to severe in nature bringing damaging wind gusts to the Neuse River and Pamlico Sound during the evening hours of July tenth.
episodes.215555: A large cluster of thunderstorms developed across the South Carolina Midlands in the early afternoon hours. These storms eventually evolved into a line and tracked to the southeast across the South Carolina Lowcountry into the early evening hours. These storms produced numerous reports of severe weather with very strong wind gusts and numerous trees down across a large area covering Colleton, Dorchester, and Charleston counties.
episodes.215562: A large cluster of thunderstorms produced a short-lived very rainfall event across the Downtown Charleston area. Automated rain gages and CoCoRaHS observers indicate that 1 to 2 inches of rain fell across the area in only 30 to 60 minutes. The intense rainfall produced a few instances of flash flooding across portions of Downtown Charleston.
episodes.215632: Slow moving frontal system provided the impetus for a long duration heavy rainfall threat that yielded significant flash flooding in Cocke County and Greene County. Additionally, a severe downburst occurred late in day in Jefferson County.
episodes.215720: A mid-level shortwave trough moved around the south side of a ridge across South-Central Texas and interacted with a warm, moist airmass. This disturbance generated thunderstorms that produced locally heavy rain leading to flash flooding.
episodes.215758: A band of thunderstorms developed during the mid to late evening hours of July 10th across southeast Kansas. This band of thunderstorms moved slowly to the southeast while training over the same areas resulting in multiple bouts of flash-flooding. In addition, a few reports of large hail up to golf ball size and damaging winds of 70 mph were relayed.
episodes.215765: An upper level low triggered scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms.  Numerous funnel clouds were reported near the I-74 corridor, with one tornado briefly touching down in a field in rural eastern McLean County.  A wet microburst flattened crops northeast of Pana late in the evening.
episodes.216159: Strong afternoon heating within a weakly sheared, moist environment leads to a strongly unstable environment coupled with steep low level lapse rates supportive of a cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms that produces numerous strong and several severe marine wind gusts as it overspreads adjacent coastal waters while moving northwestward across southwest and west central Florida.
episodes.216182: Behind a weakening morning line of showers, afternoon isolated storms developed, which produced downed trees across Johnston and Franklin Counties.
episodes.216197: Multiple rounds of severe thunderstorms moved through Missouri on July 9 and into the morning of July 10. The first round of severe thunderstorms came through portions of west central and central Missouri during the morning of July 9. This cluster of thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph winds, resulting in damage to numerous trees. A second round produced severe thunderstorms over central into south central Missouri on the evening and night of July 9 into the morning of July 10. This resulted in a brief tornado in Rolla, in addition to a few instances of flash flooding. Localized rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches were observed from Maries through Dent counties.
episodes.216333: An upper high was located near the southern Arizona/California border with north to northeast flow across the region.  Storms developed off of the higher terrain and pushed onto the lowlands, bringing wind gusts over 70 mph and some blowing dust to the Lordsburg Playa.
episodes.216492: Another day with moisture streaming around a high pressure system to southwest would bring additional thunderstorms to the eastern plains. Some of the stronger cluster of storms would go on to produce severe wind gusts.
episodes.216543: A stationary frontal boundary took up residency over the Central Appalachians beginning on July 10th, supplying ample moisture for multiple days of heavy rain over West Virginia. Showers and thunderstorms, mainly observed during peak heating hours, promoted instances of flash flooding from July 11th to July 12th over the southern half of the state. Impassable roadways due to high water were the main impacts from this stretch of heavy rain, with water receding by the evening each day once convective activity came to an end.
episodes.216546: Back to back days of flash flooding occurred in Buchanan County on July 11th and 12th as a result of a nearby frontal boundary. The front parked itself over the Central Appalachians during this time, providing the necessary components of moisture and instability to stir up daily showers and storms in the region. Activity in southwest Virginia was observed during the mornings on both of these days, and resulted in brief road closures due to high water. The front gained momentum once again and departed offshore heading into the middle of July, which limited the flooding threat and brought the return of dry weather for a few days in southwest Virginia.
episodes.216548: Showers and thunderstorms permeating around a stationary frontal boundary resulted in daily high water issues across the Ohio Valley and Central Appalachians around July 11th. Ample moisture and lift supplied by the nearby front worked in tandem with summertime heat to stir up afternoon convection as a result. In southeast Ohio, only one instance of flash flooding was observed during this time in Morgan County, where local street flooding took place on the morning of July 11th in McConnelsville. The front distanced itself from the region by the evening of July 12th, bringing the flood threat over the region to the end.
episodes.216612: During the evening hours of July 10th, a cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms moved east to southeast across portions of east-central Colorado. Estimated wind gusts up to 65 mph and one-inch diameter hail were both reported in Cheyenne County.
episodes.216758: An upper-level ridge over the southern United States began retreating westward on July 11th as a mid-level trough deepened across the southeastern states. Local thunderstorm coverage increased as convection shifted inland from the coastal waters and interacted with the sea breeze and other mesoscale boundaries near Lake Pontchartrain. Slow-moving and locally redeveloping thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall across the New Orleans and Baton Rouge metros during the early afternoon, resulting in flash flooding of several roadways and vehicles.
episodes.216759: An upper-level ridge over the southern United States began retreating westward on July 11th as a mid-level trough deepened across the southeastern states. Seabreeze convergent boundaries were the focal point for thunderstorm development in the coastal waters. A storm over Lake Pontchartrain strengthened enough to produce severe wind gusts along the lake.
episodes.216839: Throughout much of the afternoon and evening on July 8th, severe storms moved slowly through northeast Iowa with several inches of rain in some locations. This resulted in isolated flash flooding along with rises into flood stage along portions of the Cedar and Upper Iowa River basins. Additionally, these storms produced severe wind gusts which resulted in scattered instances of tree damage.
episodes.216897: Upper level troughing remained over southwest Louisiana during multiple days in mid July. This allowed scattered storms to develop each day with some producing heavy rain.
episodes.217105: From July 11th into the 12th, a slow-moving mid-level trough and surface front was draped across the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys, providing the conditions for a period of unsettled weather. During the afternoon hours on July 11th, daytime heating allowed temperatures to rise into the mid-to-upper 80s, with dew point temperatures in the low-to-mid 70s, creating a typical summertime unstable environment with between 1500 and 2500 J/kg of mixed-layer CAPE. While the mid- and upper-level disturbance over the region was not particularly amplified, it did allow a band of 30 knot mid-level winds to set up over south central Kentucky, which supported effective bulk shear values of 30-35 knots. Scattered multicell thunderstorms produced a few instances of wind damage in Warren and Barren County, with storms gradually weakening during the late evening hours on the 11th. However, overnight from the 11th into the 12th, as a cutoff low pivoted slowly across the area, slow-moving showers and thunderstorms continued to produce areas of flash flooding across central and southern Kentucky. Decreasing, but sufficient instability and precipitable water values near or over 2 inches resulted in efficient rainfall producing showers and storms which finally began to dissipate during the evening hours on July 12th.
episodes.217137: Numerous thunderstorms and scattered storm clusters developed across the North Carolina foothills and Piedmont throughout the afternoon and evening. Multiple severe thunderstorms occurred, producing mainly small swaths of damaging wind gusts. An EF1 tornado was also reported across Cleveland and Lincoln Counties.
episodes.217147: Scattered-to-numerous thunderstorms and storm clusters moved across upstate South Carolina throughout the morning into the early afternoon. A few brief damaging wind gusts were reported.
episodes.217148: A slow moving front produced scattered thunderstorms across southeastern PA and NJ. This included storms on July 11 that produced a series of microbursts, particularly in Montgomery County and Philadelphia.
episodes.217160: A slow moving front produced scattered thunderstorms across southeastern PA and NJ.
episodes.217183: An inverted lower tropospheric trough associated with an upper trough of low pressure moved west through the Florida Keys and adjacent coastal waters during the afternoon and evening hours of July 10, 2026.  Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed over the Straits of Florida and Cuba, with resultant outflow boundaries focusing new development of showers and thunderstorms inside the reef tract and across the Florida Keys.  Numerous gale-force wind gusts were measured in association with the stronger thunderstorms and outflow boundaries.
episodes.217198: During the evening of July 11th, a small non-supercell thunderstorm produced a tornado or landspout tornado at Moredock Lake. The tornado caused no damage and was confirmed via video footage.
episodes.217225: An upper trough over the Mid Mississippi Valley moved south during the day on July 11, 2026. The trough interacted with a moist and unstable airmass across the Mid-South. Mid-level lapse rates greater than 7.5 C/km and MLCAPEs greater than 2500 J/kg helped to feed storms that developed over southeast Missouri by late morning. Bulk Shear values of 20 to 30 knots helped support storm organization. Storms moving into the area from southeast Missouri eventually formed into an east-west line by early afternoon, with several reports of damaging winds across Arkansas and West Tennessee.
episodes.217226: An upper trough over the Mid Mississippi Valley moved south during the day on July 11, 2026. The trough interacted with a moist and unstable airmass across the Mid-South. episodes.217282: An upper level disturbance arrived and lingered over South Florida and the adjacent waters in early to mid June which produced a period of unsettled weather.
episodes.217291: Continuing an active monsoon period with multiple recorded wind gusts of 50 to 81 mph in Pima, Pinal, Greenlee, Graham, and Cochise counties. The severe thunderstorm winds caused damage across the Tucson Metro an in Lavender Farms . Additionally, the heavy rainfall caused running washes that led to 3 water rescues in the Tucson Metro and impassable roadways.
episodes.217449: A fairly well-organized cluster of strong thunderstorms moved southeast across far southeastern Colorado into adjacent far southwestern Kansas late in the evening of July 10th. Most of the peak wind gusts from personal weather stations were in the 45 to 55 mph range, however one severe wind gust was reported near Johnson from this line of storms.
